records.name: Witness to Innocence
records.summary: An advocacy group led by people who were cleared of their convictions after time on death row, together with their family members. It campaigns to end the death penalty and helps exonerated people and their families after release.
records.what_you_do: Get email updates, take action on campaign alerts, ask an exoneree to speak to your group, or give to support the work.

cost.text: Email updates and action alerts are free. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for email updates on the group's site, or open an action alert from the Action Alerts button to take part in a campaign.
first_step.basis: Email updates, action alerts and speaker requests are open to anyone, and the site gives a clear way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists no regular meetings or in person events, so a first visit happens online. You read a campaign page, take an action alert, or sign up for updates, and the listed actions cost nothing (donations are optional).
first_visit_tips: Start online: the site lists no visiting hours.
To ask for a speaker, email speakers@witnesstoinnocence.org; the page does not say how far ahead to book.

records.notes: Deep pass on the join and Speakers Bureau pages. Speaker requests go by email (speakers@witnesstoinnocence.org) or the Speaker Inquiry Form; the budget is agreed with the host and no fee or lead time is published. No accessibility or visiting information is published. The newest dated item is a May 2025 post on the homepage.

records.name: Women Healed for a Purpose
records.summary: Helps women learn more about themselves and grow in confidence. Each year it hosts a daylong conference, and women can register to attend or sign up to volunteer.
records.what_you_do: Register for the yearly L.I.F.E. conference, sign up to help run it, or support the group with a donation.

schedule.text: Yearly L.I.F.E. conference on a Saturday, 11 am to 3 pm.

locations.label: Conference venue (Brand New Life Christian Center)

cost.text: The yearly conference costs $30 per person and includes a light brunch.

first_step.how: Register for the October 17, 2026 conference through the Google form on the conference page. The fee is $30 per person.
first_step.basis: The conference takes registration through a clear online form, but the page does not say how newcomers are welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The conference is one Saturday, from 11 am to 3 pm, at Brand New Life Christian Center on Germantown Avenue. A light brunch is served, and the 2026 theme is Year of Discovery; the page does not describe the sessions or speakers. The fee is $30 per person.
first_visit_tips: Register before the day through the Google form; the page does not say whether you can pay at the door.
The page does not mention parking or transit, so check the address before you go.

records.notes: Deep pass. The conference page gives the 2026 date, hours, venue, the $30 fee and the brunch. The volunteer form asks for name, email and phone, with an optional event choice, and lists no duties or time needed. The footer year 2024 is copyright and was not used as evidence. The schedule text no longer names the one dated event.

records.name: Women's Nonprofit Leadership Initiative
records.summary: Researches who sits on the boards of Greater Philadelphia's largest colleges and hospitals, and pushes for more women and people of color in those seats. Anyone can use its ready-made letters to board leaders and its tips for joining a board.
records.what_you_do: Send one of the model letters to a university or hospital board chair, read the tips for joining a higher education or healthcare board, or sign up for the mailing list to follow the research.

first_step.how: Download a model letter from the Get Involved page and send it to a university or hospital board chair.
first_step.basis: Model letters, board tips and the mailing list are open to anyone, and the site gives a clear way in. It describes no member events or volunteer roles.
first_step.what_to_expect: There is no meeting or event listed on the site, so a first step happens online. Most people start by reading the group's research on who sits on large hospital and university boards, then sending a letter to a board leader. The site lists no cost for the letters, the board tips or the mailing list.
first_visit_tips: Choose the model letter that fits the institution: higher education or healthcare.
The model letters can go to a board chair, a university president, or another board leader.

records.notes: Deep pass. Model letters, the board join tips and the mailing list are confirmed on the Get Involved page. The site lists no events and no office address, so the address above comes only from the IRS listing. The newest dated item is a July 2024 press entry on the events page, so status is dormant; tier 1 had probably_active. One web search for newer dated items found none. Whether a dormant group with a working letter tool stays listed is a decision for the owner.

records.name: Xiente
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps families move up through education, housing, workforce and money skills programs. It runs community leadership, youth and volunteer programs, and it hosts homebuyer and housing workshops.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer roles include mentoring a youth or adult in career exploration, supporting early education or after school programs, helping run networking and advocacy events, and serving on a community advisory group. You can also join the community leadership or networking programs, or register for a workshop.

schedule.text: The site does not show a schedule for its programs. Workshops are posted one at a time on the events page.

cost.text: No fee is listed for the programs or workshops we checked.

first_step.how: Fill in the short volunteer form on the Volunteer with Xiente page so the team can follow up with you.
first_step.basis: The volunteer sign-up is a short form with a follow up, and workshops are open to the public with registration. The site describes no beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteering starts with a short online form, and the team follows up from there. Some workshops are online, such as the pre-purchase housing workshop on November 12, 2026, which runs on Zoom from 5:30 to 7:30 pm Eastern after you register. The pages we checked list no fee, and spots for workshops may be limited.
first_visit_tips: Register through the link on a workshop page; the Zoom details arrive by email.
For questions about in person visits, call the main office at (215) 426-8734; the site does not describe what a visit involves.

records.notes: Deep pass. Confirmed: the volunteer form, the community leadership page (residents are the main focus; no application steps, cohort dates or cost are given), and the November 12, 2026 pre-purchase workshop (online on Zoom, registration required). The October 22, 2026 first-time homebuyer workshop is listed on the homepage as an open, Spanish-titled event; its own page was not read. The events page is very long: only its first 100,000 of about 875,000 characters were read, and they held no dated events beyond a 2026 caption, so the events list may be incomplete. The accessibility statement at xiente.org/accessibility-statement/ names another organization's email and covers website features only, so no access facts were taken from it. Tier 1 said most programs use a third-party registration form; that was not confirmed and has been removed.

records.name: Young Artist Program (YAP)
records.summary: A no-cost arts program that explores social justice through art-making for young people ages 14 to 25 in Philadelphia. It is aimed at BIPOC LGBTQ+ youth and allies.
records.what_you_do: Apply through the form on the site, then join weekly studio sessions to make art with other young people.

schedule.text: Weekly sessions Wednesday to Friday, 4 to 6:30 pm during the school year. The summer schedule, June to August, is different and is shown only as images on the site.

locations.label: Studio in the Northern Liberties area (address not listed)

cost.text: Free. Donations and a supply wishlist are optional.

first_step.how: Fill in the application on the Google form linked from the Join page on theyap.org. Applications are taken all year.
first_step.basis: A free program with a public application form that is open all year. The site does not say whether art experience is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions run Wednesday to Friday from 4 to 6:30 pm during the school year, and once you have applied you can drop in. You make art with other young people, look at social justice ideas through your work, and sometimes join guest artist workshops and gallery visits. The program is free, and participants can also get food, art supplies and the chance to sell their artwork.
first_visit_tips: Apply first; the site lists no set deadline, so check the form for current dates.
The site gives no street address for the studio, so ask the group on Instagram before your first session.
Summer sessions run on a different schedule, shown only as images, so ask before June.

records.notes: Deep pass. The Join page confirms eligibility (ages 14 to 25), a year round application form, and free sessions that take drop ins once you have applied. The events page names a 2025 Philly Zine Fest appearance as its newest dated item, so the year alone is recorded. The page footer reads 2021 next to a placeholder name, which looks like a template, so the site may be out of date; the Instagram account was not checked. Annual events named on the events page with no dates: Gay Field Day (every October), Philly Zine Fest (date not given), and Winter Art Market (every December). The summer schedule appears only in images.

records.name: YPE Philly
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a national network for young professionals in the energy industry. It is open to anyone interested in energy work in the Philadelphia area and nearby region, and it holds a monthly networking gathering.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly gathering on the second Wednesday, 6 to 8 pm, at City Tap House Logan Square. The events page lists it as YPE Philly with Green Drinks Philly. Register for each one through the Eventbrite link on that page.

schedule.text: Monthly gathering on the second Wednesday, 6 to 8 pm, at City Tap House Logan Square

first_step.how: Register for the next monthly gathering through the Eventbrite link on the group's events page.
first_step.basis: Open to anyone interested in energy work, with a sign up step for each event. The site describes no beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: The gathering is a networking evening at City Tap House Logan Square on the second Wednesday from 6 to 8 pm. The group is open to anyone interested in energy work, and the crowd is professionals and young adults. The events page gives no cost, and it says registration is required.
first_visit_tips: Register first through the Eventbrite link, since the events page says registration is required.
The page does not say whether non-members pay to attend, so check the Eventbrite listing before you go.

records.notes: Deep pass. The events page shows one recurring gathering, co-hosted with Green Drinks Philly, with registration required through Eventbrite. Tier 1 said drop in; the events page says registration is required, so drop_in is now false. The Join page gives no membership or attendance details. No dated event or news item is shown, so the status rests on the working site.

records.name: YEAH Philly
records.summary: A Black-led nonprofit that works with young people ages 15 to 24 in West and Southwest Philadelphia. It supports youth affected by violence and runs a weekday hangout, violence prevention work, and youth volunteer and work openings.
records.what_you_do: Stop by the hangout on a weekday afternoon or evening, or ask about volunteer and work openings. The group also publishes news and videos about youth issues.

schedule.text: Hangout open Monday to Friday, 2 to 10 pm. Saturdays are for scheduled events only. Closed Sunday. Ages 15 to 24.

first_step.how: Go to the hangout at 5257 Walton Ave on a weekday between 2 and 10 pm, or email teens@yeahphilly.org to ask about joining.
first_step.basis: The site posts hangout hours and an address but no intake steps. It describes its youth as teens and young adults affected by violence, so confirm by phone or email first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The hangout is open on weekdays from 2 to 10 pm, and Saturdays are for scheduled events only. The site does not say what happens on a first visit, whether you sign in, or what it costs, so the staff are the best source. When we read it, the Work with YEAH page listed no open internships or volunteer roles.
first_visit_tips: Call (267) 892-3538 or email teens@yeahphilly.org to check the fit before you go.
Go on a weekday, since the hangout is closed on Sundays and open only for scheduled events on Saturdays.
The site does not mention parking or transit, so check the street address before you go.

records.notes: Deep pass. Hours, address, phone and email are confirmed on the homepage. The newest dated item is a January 27, 2025 news piece; the 2025 footer is copyright and was not used as evidence. The events page lists only January 2024 past events and no upcoming ones. The site says the program serves youth affected by violence; that is written as a service focus, not a joining rule, so the audience stays public, but intake rules should be confirmed by phone. No SEPTA stop is named on the site, so none is listed.

leads_only.name: Green Drinks Philly
leads_only.note: Co-hosts the monthly YPE Philly gathering, per the events page. No link to its own website on that page, so not fetched in this wave.

leads_only.name: The Soapbox Community Print Shop & Zine Library
leads_only.note: Named as the host of Philly Zine Fest on the YAP events page. No link to its own website there, so not fetched in this wave.

leads_only.name: Mural Arts (Philadelphia)
leads_only.note: A Mural Arts collaboration is mentioned in an undated YEAH news item. No link to its own website there, so not fetched in this wave.

leads_only.name: Brand New Life Christian Center
leads_only.note: The conference venue for Women Healed for a Purpose. A congregation and a place, not checked in this wave.

notes: Seven groups, deep pass, 1 of 1 web search used, 27 of 60 fetches used. Status changes from tier 1: Women's Nonprofit Leadership Initiative is now dormant (newest dated item July 2024; one search found nothing newer). Xiente and Women Healed are active. YAP, YPE and YEAH stay probably_active. First step changes: YPE needs registration (not drop in); YAP needs an application first; Xiente is online_ok because the November workshop is on Zoom. Dated events were removed from schedule text for Women Healed and Xiente. Xiente's events page is about 875,000 characters and only the first 100,000 were read. Xiente's accessibility statement names another organization's email, so it was not used for access facts. Rule 7 check: none of the three partner leads had a link to its own website on the page that named it, so none were fetched; they remain leads. Process note: I made one accidental call to a docs tool (a guide menu call with empty items). It returned only a menu, created nothing, and I made no further calls to it.
